name: aRepr
doc: This is an instance of Repr which is used to provide the repr() function described below. Changing the attributes of this object will affect the size limits used by repr() and the Python debugger.

name: recursive_repr
doc: Decorator to make a repr function return fillvalue for a recursive call

name: Repr
signatures: Repr(*, maxlevel=6, maxtuple=6, maxlist=6, maxarray=5, maxdict=4, maxset=6, maxfrozenset=6, maxdeque=6, maxstring=30, maxlong=40, maxother=30, fillvalue='...', indent=None)
doc: Class which provides formatting services useful in implementing functions similar to the built-in repr(); size limits for different object types are added to avoid the generation of representations which are excessively long.

changed.text: Allow attributes to be set via keyword arguments.

name: repr
doc: This is the repr() method of aRepr. It returns a string similar to that returned by the built-in function of the same name, but with limits on most sizes.

name: fillvalue
doc: This string is displayed for recursive references. It defaults to ....

name: indent
doc: If this attribute is set to None (the default), the output is formatted with no line breaks or indentation, like the standard repr(). For example:

name: maxarray
doc: Limits on the number of entries represented for the named object type. The default is 4 for maxdict, 5 for maxarray, and 6 for the others.

name: maxdeque
doc: Limits on the number of entries represented for the named object type. The default is 4 for maxdict, 5 for maxarray, and 6 for the others.

name: maxdict
doc: Limits on the number of entries represented for the named object type. The default is 4 for maxdict, 5 for maxarray, and 6 for the others.

name: maxfrozenset
doc: Limits on the number of entries represented for the named object type. The default is 4 for maxdict, 5 for maxarray, and 6 for the others.

name: maxlevel
doc: Depth limit on the creation of recursive representations. The default is 6.

name: maxlist
doc: Limits on the number of entries represented for the named object type. The default is 4 for maxdict, 5 for maxarray, and 6 for the others.

name: maxlong
doc: Maximum number of characters in the representation for an integer. Digits are dropped from the middle. The default is 40.

name: maxother
doc: This limit is used to control the size of object types for which no specific formatting method is available on the Repr object. It is applied in a similar manner as maxstring. The default is 20.

name: maxset
doc: Limits on the number of entries represented for the named object type. The default is 4 for maxdict, 5 for maxarray, and 6 for the others.

name: maxstring
doc: Limit on the number of characters in the representation of the string. Note that the “normal” representation of the string is used as the character source: if escape sequences are needed in the representation, these may be mangled when the representation is shortened. The default is 30.

name: maxtuple
doc: Limits on the number of entries represented for the named object type. The default is 4 for maxdict, 5 for maxarray, and 6 for the others.

name: repr
doc: The equivalent to the built-in repr() that uses the formatting imposed by the instance.

name: repr1
doc: Recursive implementation used by repr(). This uses the type of obj to determine which formatting method to call, passing it obj and level. The type-specific methods should call repr1() to perform recursive formatting, with level - 1 for the value of level in the recursive call.
